question.text: Which of the following correctly describes a Sovereign Gold Bond (SGB)?

answer.text: A physical gold bar issued by the Reserve Bank of India
A government security denominated in grams of gold, offering interest and linked to gold price
A gold ETF managed by a mutual fund company
A derivative contract on gold traded on commodity exchanges

explanation.text: The Logic: Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) are government securities issued by the Reserve Bank of India on behalf of the Government of India and denominated in grams of gold. Investors pay an issue price linked to the prevailing gold price, the bond pays periodic interest, and at maturity the redemption value tracks the then-prevailing gold price. Functionally, the investor gets exposure to gold's price movement plus a coupon, without holding any physical metal. The Trap: SGBs are not physical bars — they are paper/electronic instruments issued by the RBI, not a physical product. Gold ETFs are mutual-fund-managed schemes that hold gold (or gold-backed instruments) and trade on exchanges; they are not government securities. Exchange-traded gold derivatives are commodity contracts (futures/options) and are structurally different from a sovereign bond. Note: The cited workbook (NISM Series XV — Research Analyst Workbook, pages 24, 35, 65, 73, 234, 235) discusses Electronic Gold Receipts, Gold ETFs, and references an SGB order-book example for liquidity risk, but does not contain the specific SGB definition, interest rate, redemption-price linkage, tax, lock-in, or tenure claims. The framing above is based on the RBI/Government of India SGB scheme as commonly published.
